findings.issue_text: DI wiring not updated for changed provider signatures: ProvideAnonDBStore and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService changed shape (new int64 deviceLimit and db.DB parameters replacing the anonstore.AnonStore dependency), but the diff contains no wire_gen.go regeneration or fx module updates, risking compile breaks from stale generated code, fx container build failure from an unsupplied bare int64 provider, and silent loss of the anonstore.AnonStore binding for other consumers (packages, enterprise, tests).

Device limit is not enforced atomically in CreateOrUpdateDevice: CountDevices and the subsequent INSERT/UPDATE are two independent statements with no transaction, row lock, or DB-level cap, so under a concurrent burst of first-time devices every request reads count < limit and inserts, permanently overshooting the limit by up to (concurrency − 1) until devices lapse.

Panic isolation removed from the auth path: the deleted goroutine carried a defer recover() explicitly labeled 'Tag anon session panic', and making the call synchronous without relocating that recover means a panic in getOrCreateTaggedDevice, header/IP parsing, or store code now propagates out of Anonymous.Authenticate into the authn/middleware stack, turning previously-successful anonymous requests into 500s.

Tagging moved onto the synchronous critical path with request-scoped context and no timeout: the old fire-and-forget design used context.Background() with a 2-minute timeout, but now every uncached anonymous request blocks on up to two DB round-trips, so DB contention or pool exhaustion stalls anonymous page loads, a canceled request context silently drops the device write (undercounting usage and later re-tagging the device as new), and a hung connection can pin the request with no bound.

updateDevice window is anchored to caller-supplied UpdatedAt with only +1min headroom: the WHERE clause derives bounds from a value the caller fabricated rather than the DB clock, so if an app-server instance's clock is more than 1 minute ahead when it last wrote updated_at, another instance updating the same device gets rowsAffected == 0 → ErrDeviceLimitReached, hard-rejecting an existing active device with a misattributed error message.

No negative caching for rejected devices: the 29-minute local cache is only populated after a successful write, so a device rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached never gets cached and re-executes CountDevices plus the doomed UPDATE (two queries) on every request indefinitely from exactly the bot/scraper population the limit exists to shed, turning the protection into a self-inflicted query amplifier during floods.

args slice mutated inside the WithDbSession callback in CreateOrUpdateDevice: `args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)` reassigns the captured variable inside the callback, so if the session helper re-invokes the callback on retry (e.g., connection/deadlock failure), query is prepended again and becomes a bind parameter; use dbSession.Exec(query, args...) with args left unmangled instead.

New integration test TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit sets UpdatedAt but not CreatedAt in the Device literal, writing 0001-01-01 00:00:00 into created_at, which is outside MySQL's DATETIME range (starts at 1000-01-01) and should fail under MySQL integration CI even though SQLite/Postgres accept it locally.
ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned raw from Authenticate; verify the authn error handler maps it to a meaningful 4xx rather than a bare 500 so blocked anonymous users get an actionable response.
AnonymousDeviceLimit accepts negative config values, which the deviceLimit > 0 gate silently treats as unlimited; consider validating the configuration.

anonymousDeviceExpiration (30 * 24 * time.Hour) is now defined independently in both the anonstore and api packages; if either horizon is changed without the other, the admin device list and the limit/count windows will silently disagree.

TOCTOU race in CreateOrUpdateDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:~113–128): the CountDevices limit check and the subsequent insert/upsert are separate DB round trips with no transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or constraint-based guard, so concurrent unauthenticated requests can all observe count < limit and all insert new device rows, overshooting the configured cap and causing unbounded anon_device table growth

Synchronous, unbounded DB work on the anonymous auth hot path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:~44–50): the async goroutine and its 2-minute timeout were removed so TagDevice now runs inline in Authenticate, and CreateOrUpdateDevice adds a COUNT query (over anon_device filtered only by the 30-day updated_at window) before every upsert on every cache miss; an unauthenticated client can rotate the User-Agent header to bypass the per-device cache, turning every request into a synchronous COUNT + insert attempt with no explicit timeout — a new unauthenticated DoS/latency-amplification surface against the database

Device identity is attacker-mintable, enabling quota-exhaustion lockout (anonimpl/impl.go TagDevice/device-ID derivation + anonstore/database.go CreateOrUpdateDevice): device IDs derive from client-controlled inputs (User-Agent/IP) with no rate limiting on new device creation, so a single unauthenticated attacker can fill the entire device_limit quota in minutes with unique UAs and hold all slots indefinitely with cheap keep-alive requests (rows held 30 days), causing every legitimate new anonymous visitor to be rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached — a fail-closed one-actor kill switch for anonymous access

updateDevice (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:~96–107) conflates RowsAffected() == 0 with ErrDeviceLimitReached: zero affected rows is not an existence check — (a) on MySQL without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS a matched-but-unchanged UPDATE reports 0 rows, so if updated_at truncates to the same stored value a legitimate active device is misclassified and rejected; (b) the BETWEEN updated_at-30d AND updated_at+1m window is sensitive to inter-instance clock skew >1 minute, failing to match rows written by an ahead node; (c) any driver-level anomaly returning 0 surfaces as an auth rejection rather than a retriable write error

CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:109-115) runs CountDevices — an O(N) aggregate over all devices updated in the last 30 days — before every write, making steady-state DB load quadratic (~N² row visits per 29-minute window); if anon_device.updated_at has no index, the COUNT degrades to a full table scan per tag

Once the device limit is reached, every rejected CreateOrUpdateDevice request still costs two queries (COUNT + no-op UPDATE) with no negative caching, backoff, or rate limit, so enabling the protection increases DB load exactly under a flood of unique device IDs instead of shedding it

TagDevice was moved from a fire-and-forget background goroutine to a synchronous call inside Anonymous.Authenticate (client.go:44-50, impl.go:144-149), so every anonymous auth with a local-cache miss now blocks on 1-2 inline DB round trips and occupies HTTP handler concurrency slots that previously stayed free
The independent 2-minute context.Background() timeout for device tagging was removed, so a slow query or exhausted connection pool can stall anonymous requests up to pool/request timeouts
The removed recover() means a panic in the tag path now surfaces as an anonymous auth request failure instead of being contained
Tying device tagging to the request context means a client disconnect mid-write cancels the tag, causing devices to be under-recorded

Check-then-act race in CreateOrUpdateDevice (database.go:108-115): CountDevices and the insert run on separate sessions with no transaction, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, advisory lock, or constraint, so concurrent requests all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, letting the device limit overrun by the burst size and making enforcement only correct for serial traffic

ListDevices (api/api.go:70-75) loads every device from the last 30 days into memory with no limit or pagination; with large intended device_limit configurations this admin endpoint materializes and JSON-serializes the whole active table per call

updateDevice (database.go:95-96) conflates rowsAffected == 0 with ErrDeviceLimitReached; zero rows can also result from multi-node clock skew failing the updated_at <= device.UpdatedAt + 1 minute upper bound, the cleanup job deleting a counted row between the COUNT and the UPDATE, or a returning device whose row is older than the 30-day window, producing spurious mislabeled rejections of anonymous auth

Anonymous authentication is now synchronously coupled to the database: the isolation layer (goroutine, context.Background() with 2-minute timeout, panic recovery) was deleted, so anonymous requests with a cold per-instance cache block the auth path on CountDevices + CreateOrUpdateDevice — even when the device limit is unconfigured (device_limit = 0 default) on existing deployments. DB slowness now stalls anonymous auth with no timeout bound replacing the removed 2-minute cap, and request cancellation can abort the tag write mid-flight (lost tracking, and the local cache is only set on success so it retries every request).

ErrDeviceLimitReached crosses the authn boundary as a raw store error with no HTTP status/authn-error mapping: the authn framework only special-cases ErrNoIdentity, so the bare fmt.Errorf("device limit reached") from Anonymous.Authenticate is surfaced as a generic authentication failure with internal error text, hard-locking every new anonymous device out of all anonymous routes (including the sign-in UX page) with no deliberate status code, response body, or UX contract.

Persistent anonymous-lockout vector: device IDs are client-controlled (cookie/header-supplied), so an unauthenticated attacker can fabricate device IDs to exhaust the limit and deny service to genuinely new anonymous devices for up to 30 days (until rows age out or DeleteDevicesOlderThan cleans up); there is no rate limiting, challenge, or eviction for garbage devices on this externally reachable boundary.

The device limit is not enforced atomically — count-then-insert race: CountDevices and the subsequent insert/update in anonstore/database.go are separate, non-transactional statements, so concurrent first-time requests from distinct devices all observe count < deviceLimit and all insert, overshooting the configured limit (potentially far beyond it under burst/bot traffic); no row lock, transaction, or unique-slot mechanism guards the check.

MySQL RowsAffected semantics can produce a false "device limit reached" for an existing, in-window device: go-sql-driver/mysql reports rows changed, not matched (no clientFoundRows), so if the UPDATE sets identical client_ip/user_agent/updated_at (e.g., same-second re-tag with same IP/UA across pods, since the 29-min cache is per-instance and MySQL DATETIME truncates sub-second precision), RowsAffected() returns 0 and a legitimate device is blocked; Postgres/SQLite count matched rows so behavior diverges across supported databases and sqlite integration tests can't catch it.

Public provider signatures changed with no visible wire/DI updates, making AnonStore no longer injectable: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes (sqlStore, deviceLimit int64) and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService hard-codes the concrete *AnonDBStore, but the diff contains no wire set / wire_gen.go changes — if the provider remains in a wire set, generation fails (nothing provides a bare int64); if removed, AnonStore can no longer be bound/substituted via DI and downstream consumers (e.g., enterprise) that provided their own AnonStore break silently or at compile time.

A required (non-optional) property was added to the published GrafanaConfig interface: `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined` uses `| undefined` instead of `?`, so any external implementer constructing a GrafanaConfig-typed object in @grafana/data now fails type-check unless they add the key; additionally the type never matches the actual wire format since the Go DTO (FrontendSettingsDTO, no omitempty) always emits an integer (0 = unlimited).

TagDevice's public error contract changed for all callers, not just the one updated: it previously swallowed tagDeviceUI failures (best-effort by design) but now propagates every store error at anonimpl/impl.go:147, while the AnonDeviceAPI kind and any other call sites (OSS or downstream) still assume best-effort semantics and would now fail on transient DB errors; all callers of this exported method need auditing.

Missing timeout on the now-synchronous DB work in the anonymous auth hot path: the PR deletes the fire-and-forget goroutine that had an explicit `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)` and calls `a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` inline in `Authenticate` (client.go:44-49), with no deadline added anywhere down the stack (TagDevice → tagDeviceUI → CountDevices + upsert/update) and Grafana's HTTP server setting no default read/write timeout, so a hung or slow database now stalls anonymous requests indefinitely instead of being bounded at 2 minutes
A DB outage now produces a Warn log line per anonymous request with no sampling or backoff, causing a log flood

Device limit check is not atomic (TOCTOU): `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (database.go ~103-118) performs `CountDevices(...)` as a standalone statement and then separately performs the upsert when `count < deviceLimit`, with no transaction, row locking, or DB-side constraint tying the insert to the count, so concurrent cache-miss requests can all observe `count < limit` and all insert, overshooting the limit by roughly the number of in-flight requests

`updateDevice` (database.go ~89-94) treats `RowsAffected() == 0` as `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, but on MySQL `ROW_COUNT()` reports rows changed rather than rows matched (unless `clientFoundRows` is set in the DSN), so an UPDATE that matches a row but sets identical values (e.g., two instances handling parallel requests from the same device in the same second) yields 0 affected rows and spuriously rejects a legitimate, active, returning device with an auth failure

Panic containment for device tagging was removed: the previous code deliberately recovered panics from the tagging path via `defer recover()` and degraded to a warning, but the replacement has no containment, so a panic inside `TagDevice`/the store now surfaces in the authn request path

P1: The new limit-rejection branch in Anonymous.Authenticate (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-50), `if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) { return nil, err }`, has zero test coverage — the sentinel only appears in database_test.go which tests the store, not the client; no test at the service, client, authn-router, or HTTP level verifies that an anonymous request from a device beyond the limit is rejected (or with what status code — authn likely surfaces a generic 500), or that non-limit tag failures are still swallowed and auth proceeds, so if the wiring between TagDevice, Authenticate, and authn is wrong the feature silently doesn't enforce anything (or blocks the wrong requests) and no test fails.

P1: The interplay between the local cache in TagDevice and the device limit is completely unverified — a returning device within the cache TTL may bypass the DB and never see the limit error, while a cache-miss device gets rejected.

P1: The diff removed the goroutine's panic recovery and 2-minute timeout in TagDevice, making it the synchronous hot path for every anonymous request, and this behavioral change ships with no test coverage.

P1: The updateDevice success path — a returning device under the limit re-tagging successfully via rowsAffected > 0 — is untested (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers rejection of an unseen device); given the hand-built Exec arg list (`args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`) and the `BETWEEN updated_at` window, a bug there (wrong arg order, inclusive/exclusive bounds, or MySQL RowsAffected returning 0 when an UPDATE matches a row but changes no values, e.g., two updates within the same timestamp precision) would lock out every returning device with no failing test; the test should also assert the store still contains only the first device after the rejected attempt.

P2: No test verifies the `device_limit` ini key is parsed and wired into enforcement — every test bypasses configuration (the store test passes the limit directly to ProvideAnonDBStore, and impl_test.go uses setting.NewCfg() with limit 0), so a typo in the key name, a wrong section, or a wiring mistake in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService (which now constructs the store from cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit read via MustInt64(0)) leaves the feature silently inert while the entire suite stays green.

P2: Untested edge case — an existing device outside the 30-day window is rejected when the limit is reached: updateDevice only succeeds if the stored updated_at falls within `BETWEEN (now - 30d) AND (now + 1min)`, so a device last seen ~31 days ago (not yet removed by cleanup) returning while the limit is reached gets rowsAffected == 0 and ErrDeviceLimitReached even though it already exists, locking the user out until the cleanup job deletes the row; no test covers devices at/near the 30-day boundary, so it's unknown whether this lockout is intended behavior or a bug.

P2: TagDevice's error-propagation contract change is untested for its other callers — it previously swallowed all tagDeviceUI errors (log + return nil) but now returns any error, so the post-auth hook callers on the auth broker now receive errors they previously never saw (e.g., transient DB failures during a tagged login); no test asserts the intended semantics for non-limit errors on these paths or documents which errors are meant to be fatal.

P3: The limit invariant under concurrency is untested — the count-then-act gate (CountDevices < limit, then insert) allows two concurrent first-time requests to both pass the check and both insert, exceeding the configured limit; no test validates the limit under parallel requests or documents acceptable slack, leaving it unclear whether strict enforcement is required.

P3: The anonymousDeviceLimit frontend settings field has no test and no consumer — nothing would catch a JSON name mismatch between the Go DTO (AnonymousDeviceLimit, always serialized, default 0) and the TS interface (`number | undefined`, which can in fact never be undefined since the backend always emits an int); either wire up the consumer and test it, or drop the field until it's used.
Removal of the injectable store constructor in ProvideAnonymousDeviceService reduces the test seam for the anonStore.

Synchronous, un-timed DB work moved into the anonymous auth hot path: TagDevice was previously fire-and-forget in a goroutine with context.Background(), a 2-minute timeout, and panic recovery, but now runs inline on the request context with no timeout and no panic guard — every anonymous request (highest-volume unauthenticated traffic) blocks on a DB round-trip (COUNT + UPSERT/UPDATE on every cache miss) before auth completes, a slow/hung DB holds HTTP workers and shared-pool connections until anonymous traffic and then all traffic stalls, and a panic in the tag path now aborts the request instead of being absorbed (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-49)

updateDevice treats rowsAffected == 0 as the sole signal for ErrDeviceLimitReached, causing false hard auth failures for legitimate, under-limit devices: MySQL changed-rows semantics (CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS not set in the DSN) make a concurrent same-second re-tag of the same device a no-op UPDATE returning 0 rows (very reachable on cold-cache page-load bursts once the limit is saturated), and the BETWEEN updated_at - 30d AND updated_at + 1min window is computed from client-supplied device.UpdatedAt rather than DB time, so >1min clock skew between Grafana instances yields 0 rows and a false 'limit reached'; the only new test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) covers the reject path, not these false-positive or update-success paths (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-110)

Provider signatures changed with no DI/registration updates anywhere in the diff: ProvideAnonDBStore gained a primitive int64 parameter and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService swapped its anonstore.AnonStore parameter for db.DB, but no wiring files are touched — if the old registration still exists, fx cannot resolve a bare int64 (app fails to boot with 'no provider for int64'), explicit construction sites break compilation, and other consumers of the previously-injected AnonStore lose their provider; the registration file needs to be shown/verified (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:52-54, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37-40)

TOCTOU race in device-limit enforcement: CountDevices and the subsequent create/update run in separate sessions with no transaction, locking, or constraint tying the insert to the count, so N concurrent requests from new devices (or bursts across multiple instances) can all read count < limit and all insert, pushing the device count above the configured cap — needs a single transaction or dialect-appropriate conditional upsert covering count+write (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121)

Unauthenticated device-ID stuffing turns the cap into a lockout primitive with DB amplification: device IDs are client-supplied (header/cookie) and unvalidated, and tagging requires no credentials or rate limiting, so an attacker can send device_limit cheap requests with random device IDs to fill the table and cause hard auth failures for every new (or 30-day-expired) anonymous visitor for up to 30 days, effectively closing a public dashboard to new users; additionally, rejected devices are not negatively cached, so every blocked request still costs a COUNT + UPDATE round-trip, amplifying DB load — needs rate limiting, negative caching of rejections, or a soft handling path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121, client.go:45-47)

Device-limit enforcement is one fmt.Errorf("%v") away from failing open: the hard limit only works if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) survives every intermediate layer (tagDeviceUI, WithDbSession, future refactors) unwrapped, and any future wrap without %w silently degrades the limit into a warn-log-and-allow — the exact silent-pass failure mode; there is no test covering client/authn-layer enforcement (only the store), so such a regression would ship invisibly — worth an integration test asserting the 401/auth error when the limit is hit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:46, anonstore/database.go:16)

goldens.comment: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.
The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

However, the UPDATE sets only `client_ip`, `user_agent`, and `updated_at`; on MySQL (go-sql-driver/mysql default), `RowsAffected` reports changed rows, so if the values written are identical to the current row values, `RowsAffected()` can be 0 even though the row matched (e.g., same-second `updated_at` / same IP+UA). In that case the code will incorrectly return `ErrDeviceLimitReached` for a legitimate, in-window existing device, and behavior can diverge across DBs because other drivers may count matched rows differently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: The updateDevice success path — a returning device under the limit re-tagging successfully via rowsAffected > 0 — is untested (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only covers rejection of an unseen device); given the hand-built Exec arg list (`args = append([]interface{}{query}, args...)`) and the `BETWEEN updated_at` window, a bug there (wrong arg order, inclusive/exclusive bounds, or MySQL RowsAffected returning 0 when an UPDATE matches a row but changes no values, e.g., two updates within the same timestamp precision) would lock out every returning device with no failing test; the test should also assert the store still contains only the first device after the rejected attempt.

WHERE device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?` and `RowsAffected() > 0` (else returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`). adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Untested edge case — an existing device outside the 30-day window is rejected when the limit is reached: updateDevice only succeeds if the stored updated_at falls within `BETWEEN (now - 30d) AND (now + 1min)`, so a device last seen ~31 days ago (not yet removed by cleanup) returning while the limit is reached gets rowsAffected == 0 and ErrDeviceLimitReached even though it already exists, locking the user out until the cleanup job deletes the row; no test covers devices at/near the 30-day boundary, so it's unknown whether this lockout is intended behavior or a bug.

adjudication.rationale: Diff-grounded: when `deviceLimit > 0` and the recent-device count is `>= deviceLimit`, `CreateOrUpdateDevice` calls `updateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). `updateDevice` only updates rows where `device_id = ? AND updated_at BETWEEN (now-30d) AND (now+1m)`; otherwise `rowsAffected == 0` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`. So an existing device record with `updated_at` just outside the 30-day window will be rejected under limit pressure. adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: TagDevice's error-propagation contract change is untested for its other callers — it previously swallowed all tagDeviceUI errors (log + return nil) but now returns any error, so the post-auth hook callers on the auth broker now receive errors they previously never saw (e.g., transient DB failures during a tagged login); no test asserts the intended semantics for non-limit errors on these paths or documents which errors are meant to be fatal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: The limit invariant under concurrency is untested — the count-then-act gate (CountDevices < limit, then insert) allows two concurrent first-time requests to both pass the check and both insert, exceeding the configured limit; no test validates the limit under parallel requests or documents acceptable slack, leaving it unclear whether strict enforcement is required.

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go), the device limit is enforced via a non-atomic count-then-act gate: it calls `CountDevices(...)`, compares `count >= s.deviceLimit`, and only then proceeds to insert/upsert. Under concurrent requests, two goroutines can both observe `count < limit` and both insert, temporarily exceeding the configured limit. The added test `TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit` covers only the sequential case, not parallel/concurrent enforcement, and the diff contains no locking/transactional mechanism to make this invariant strict. This is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern about concurrency semantics and missing validation/documentation, but not a directly verifiable deterministic defect from the diff alone (it depends on desired strictness under concurrency).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Synchronous, un-timed DB work moved into the anonymous auth hot path: TagDevice was previously fire-and-forget in a goroutine with context.Background(), a 2-minute timeout, and panic recovery, but now runs inline on the request context with no timeout and no panic guard — every anonymous request (highest-volume unauthenticated traffic) blocks on a DB round-trip (COUNT + UPSERT/UPDATE on every cache miss) before auth completes, a slow/hung DB holds HTTP workers and shared-pool connections until anonymous traffic and then all traffic stalls, and a panic in the tag path now aborts the request instead of being absorbed (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:44-49)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the anonymous auth client changed from a fire-and-forget goroutine with panic recovery and a 2-minute timeout to an inline call on the request context: the `go func(){ ... context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), timeoutTag) ... recover() ... }` block was removed and replaced with `if err := a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...)` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go). This means authentication now waits for TagDevice’s work on cache misses, which can include DB interactions (e.g., in anonstore/database.go `CreateOrUpdateDevice` can `CountDevices` and then UPDATE/UPSERT). The finding’s core concern (hot-path blocking + no explicit timeout + no panic guard) is grounded in the diff, but it’s primarily a performance/resilience/architecture issue rather than a strictly verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: updateDevice treats rowsAffected == 0 as the sole signal for ErrDeviceLimitReached, causing false hard auth failures for legitimate, under-limit devices: MySQL changed-rows semantics (CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS not set in the DSN) make a concurrent same-second re-tag of the same device a no-op UPDATE returning 0 rows (very reachable on cold-cache page-load bursts once the limit is saturated), and the BETWEEN updated_at - 30d AND updated_at + 1min window is computed from client-supplied device.UpdatedAt rather than DB time, so >1min clock skew between Grafana instances yields 0 rows and a false 'limit reached'; the only new test (TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit) covers the reject path, not these false-positive or update-success paths (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:72-110)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go, updateDevice() treats RowsAffected()==0 as ErrDeviceLimitReached after an UPDATE ... WHERE device_id=? AND updated_at BETWEEN ? AND ?. But RowsAffected==0 can mean “row matched but no data changed” (not just “no row matched”), which is a common UPDATE behavior (notably in MySQL). Since the UPDATE sets updated_at to device.UpdatedAt, if device.UpdatedAt equals the stored updated_at (e.g., same-second/tag burst or caller reuses a timestamp), the UPDATE can legitimately be a no-op and return 0, triggering ErrDeviceLimitReached. This error now propagates to authentication: client.go returns the error when TagDevice hits ErrDeviceLimitReached, so the false-positive becomes a hard auth failure. Additionally, the BETWEEN window is computed from device.UpdatedAt (caller-provided/server-instance time) rather than DB time, so time skew can also produce 0 affected rows and the same false ErrDeviceLimitReached. The added test only asserts the rejection path when inserting a new device beyond the limit and does not cover “existing device should still update successfully under limit-saturated conditions.”

adjudication_records.issue_text: Provider signatures changed with no DI/registration updates anywhere in the diff: ProvideAnonDBStore gained a primitive int64 parameter and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService swapped its anonstore.AnonStore parameter for db.DB, but no wiring files are touched — if the old registration still exists, fx cannot resolve a bare int64 (app fails to boot with 'no provider for int64'), explicit construction sites break compilation, and other consumers of the previously-injected AnonStore lose their provider; the registration file needs to be shown/verified (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:52-54, pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go:37-40)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change provider signatures (ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64, and ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now takes db.DB and internally constructs the store). Within the diff, tests/call sites shown were updated, but no DI/module wiring changes are shown here; if the project uses fx (as the finding suggests), the wiring outside this diff may need updates to satisfy the new parameters. However, the diff alone cannot prove a boot failure because the fx registration code is not included.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race in device-limit enforcement: CountDevices and the subsequent create/update run in separate sessions with no transaction, locking, or constraint tying the insert to the count, so N concurrent requests from new devices (or bursts across multiple instances) can all read count < limit and all insert, pushing the device count above the configured cap — needs a single transaction or dialect-appropriate conditional upsert covering count+write (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121)

adjudication.rationale: In `CreateOrUpdateDevice` the limit check is implemented as `CountDevices(...)` followed by a separate create/upsert path when `count < s.deviceLimit` (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go). The count and the subsequent insert/upsert are not shown to be in a single transaction or protected by any DB constraint/locking in this diff, so concurrent requests can all observe `count < limit` and all proceed to insert, exceeding the configured cap (classic TOCTOU).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unauthenticated device-ID stuffing turns the cap into a lockout primitive with DB amplification: device IDs are client-supplied (header/cookie) and unvalidated, and tagging requires no credentials or rate limiting, so an attacker can send device_limit cheap requests with random device IDs to fill the table and cause hard auth failures for every new (or 30-day-expired) anonymous visitor for up to 30 days, effectively closing a public dashboard to new users; additionally, rejected devices are not negatively cached, so every blocked request still costs a COUNT + UPDATE round-trip, amplifying DB load — needs rate limiting, negative caching of rejections, or a soft handling path (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go:112-121, client.go:45-47)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a hard-fail path for anonymous auth once `AnonymousDeviceLimit` is reached. In `CreateOrUpdateDevice`, when `count >= s.deviceLimit` it calls `updateDevice`; if the `UPDATE ... WHERE device_id = ? ...` affects 0 rows, `updateDevice` returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached` (database.go). That error is now propagated out of `TagDevice` (`return err` added in impl.go) and in `Authenticate` it is treated as fatal (`if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) { return nil, err }` in client.go), which can block new anonymous visitors when the table is “full”. Additionally, every attempt when at the limit performs a `CountDevices` + `UPDATE` round-trip (database.go), with no negative caching in this change, creating avoidable DB load under repeated blocked attempts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Device-limit enforcement is one fmt.Errorf("%v") away from failing open: the hard limit only works if errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) survives every intermediate layer (tagDeviceUI, WithDbSession, future refactors) unwrapped, and any future wrap without %w silently degrades the limit into a warn-log-and-allow — the exact silent-pass failure mode; there is no test covering client/authn-layer enforcement (only the store), so such a regression would ship invisibly — worth an integration test asserting the 401/auth error when the limit is hit (pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go:46, anonstore/database.go:16)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, enforcement at the authn/client layer depends on `errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached)` in `pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go` to decide whether to block authentication; otherwise it only warn-logs and allows. The limit error itself is a plain `var ErrDeviceLimitReached = fmt.Errorf(...)` returned directly from the store (`updateDevice` / `CreateOrUpdateDevice`), and there is only a store-level test (`TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit`) asserting the error, not an integration test covering the client/authn enforcement path. While the finding’s “one fmt.Errorf("%v") away” part is speculative about future wrapping, the brittleness and missing higher-layer test are real, diff-grounded review concerns for this new limit logic.
